pr_body:
This supports `PWDEBUG=console` that:
- runs headed;
- disables timeouts;
- adds `playwright` console helper.

When using `PWDEBUG=anything-but-console`, we open inspector.
Docs keep suggesting `PWDEBUG=1`.

Fixes #5693.
Fixes #5840.
pr_comments: `PWDEBUG=inspector` is way too long. Are we making everyone's lives miserable because of a single user that did not want inspector gui? I'd keep docs as is, saying `PWDEBUG=1`

issue_context.title: [Question] Docs for debugging: PWDEBUG=1, page.pause() and debugger;
issue_context.body:
Release 1.9 brought us the awesome [Inspector](https://playwright.dev/docs/inspector/). E.g. we can set `PWDEBUG=1` and also set  `await page.pause();` on a page to pause at that occurence.

But the [Debugging tools](https://playwright.dev/docs/debug/) is sparse with this information, and it also mentions another way. https://playwright.dev/docs/debug/#run-in-debug-mode has [an image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/284612/86857345-299abc00-c073-11ea-9e31-02923a9f0d4b.png) that shows a `debugger;` line which I assume is VS Code specific.

As such, should the [Debugging tools](https://playwright.dev/docs/debug/) page better describe `await page.pause()` and its relation to it? And should the image rather show that than the VS Code `debugger;`? (I am assuming it is from VS Code, but could not find in the VS Code docs).
